chunks: (Shu'aib) said: "My Lord knows well what you are doing."
ai.seo_question: What did Prophet Shu'aib say about God's knowledge of human actions?
ai.summary: In the context of Surah Ash-Shu'ara, this verse (26:213) highlights Prophet Shu'aib's (peace be upon him) reliance on divine omniscience rather than human judgment when confronting the disbelievers of Madyan. Shia exegetes often view this as a model of sabr (patience) and tawakkul (trust in God), illustrating that the Prophet's role is to convey the message while God alone holds the authority to judge and punish hidden deeds.
